translate_en|mods/RadioTraders/42/media/: Master switch. Off: traders work exactly like the Base Trader. On: turns on reputation, haggling, contracts, services, Market Pressure and broadcasts (and dead drops or rare events if you switch those on). Every number scales from your Base Trader prices.
Cost to request an airdrop instead of a mailbox pickup. Default 500.
Semicolon-separated list of ammo items (Module.Item) always tradeable with Ironside, even if not in current stock. Example: Base.556Box;MarzGuns.9mmBox
Lets you trade bulk ammo you have for bulk ammo you need from Ironside, valued by caliber. Box, Carton and Crate only -- no single rounds or mags.
Percent chance per call that Sparks has it. Default 2.
Lets Sparks occasionally offer a black-market walkie-talkie found nowhere else, with exceptional range and weather resistance. Off by default.
Removes the trader picker entirely. Every call is an Open Call into static -- you find out who answers, if anyone does. Once someone picks up, Relay still works to reach someone specific.
Ironside sometimes offers a bounty on two trailer park debtors. Needs Bandits. (WIP)
Cash paid when both debtors are dead.

Multiplies the cost each time you ask the same trader again in one call. 1.0 = no increase. 1.5 = 3rd ask costs about double the 1st, 4th about triple. Resets when you hang up or get relayed elsewhere.
What it costs to ask a trader for a one-off peek at a few more things, on top of their normal shelf. Scales with the selling price multiplier like any other price.
How many extra items get revealed per bribe. Asking again later reveals different items, not repeats, until the trader's eligible pool runs dry.
0 = automatic: picks a frequency clear of every station in the world (vanilla, emergency broadcast and modded) and prints it in the server log. Set a value to force one, e.g. 105.4.
About how many announcements air per in-game day.
Traders announce deals, jobs and shortages on a real radio channel you can tune to.
Cheapest a car can be. Heavier vehicles cost more on top of this.
Vehicles Wrench never sells, separated by semicolons. A * matches part of a name. Example: Base.lambo; *m113*; *tank*
Highest condition (1 to 100) each part of a used car can roll. Rough cars (average under 45) don't start first try.
Lowest condition (1 to 100) each part of a used car can roll.
Max cars Wrench can list each restock -- the actual count is random up to this, so some restocks may have fewer or none. 0 always hides the lot.

Exact prices for specific vehicles. Format: Vehicle=Price, separated by semicolons. A * matches part of a name. Example: Base.lambo=150000; *m113*=90000. Without an override, sports cars cost 3x, military vehicles 2.5x and big trucks 1.75x.
How far away (in tiles) the delivery truck drops your car. It lands between 80 and 100 percent of this, out of sight. A green arrow points to it until you get close.
Off: Wrench only sells cars added by vehicle mods (Ki5 and others). Vanilla car parts are not affected.
Chance per call that a trader's card reader isn't working, on top of power outages and storms.
Added to every card payment. In 1993 an ATM or card network fee ran about $1.

With PZLinux installed and a Credit Card in your main inventory, traders run your card when you're short on cash. It charges your PZLinux bank balance plus a network fee. The card reader is sometimes down: during power outages, storms, or plain bad luck.

Ironside: bullets, shells and boxes (vanilla and gun mods) for every firearm the game has loaded, whether or not Firearms itself is on. Turn only this off to stop him giving out ammo but still let him sell the guns.
Ironside: bayonets and suppressors (rare, priced accordingly). Vanilla and gun mods.
Homestead: tools, nails, screws, planks, rope. Turning a category off removes its items; a trader with nothing left goes off the air.
Ranger: camping and outdoor gear. Turning a category off removes its items; a trader with nothing left goes off the air.
Threads: everyday clothing swept in from vanilla and any clothing mod (Authentic Z included), plus rare protective gear like vests and helmets.
On/off switch for Night Owl's DrugTime89 cocaine/crack trading plus the Contraband Items/Buys lists below. Off by default since it depends on mods you may not have installed.
On/off switch for everything listed in Custom Items and Custom Buys below, without needing to clear the text out.
Sparks: batteries, electronics, radios. Turning a category off removes its items; a trader with nothing left goes off the air.
Homestead: seeds and gardening supplies. Turning a category off removes its items; a trader with nothing left goes off the air.
Ironside: every ranged weapon the game has loaded, vanilla and gun mods (Guns of Marz, etc). Turn this off to keep Ironside's ammo trade while blocking outright gun purchases.
Night Owl: canned and shelf-stable food. Turning a category off removes its items; a trader with nothing left goes off the air.
Ranger: always buys jewelry, gems and precious metals, and pays for trophies, collectibles and other found valuables, priced by rarity. Buy-only, apart from the odd gold bar.
Ironside: magazines, clips and speedloaders for every firearm that needs one, vanilla and gun mods (Guns of Marz, etc), independent of the Ammo toggle.

Doc: bandages, medicine, first-aid items (incl. modded), Water Purification Tablets, and cure items such as the Knox Antidote mod if installed. Turning a category off removes its items; a trader with nothing left goes off the air.
Ironside: crowbars, machetes and other melee weapons. Independent of the Firearms and Ammo toggles.
Homestead: pet food, pet meds and gear, plus Companion Dogs, CD: Cats and Horse Mod items when those mods are installed.

Wrench: vehicle tools and a rotating selection of vehicle parts, including modded vehicles such as KI5's. Used cars have their own settings further down. Turning a category off removes its items; a trader with nothing left goes off the air.
Chance per call to Night Owl.
Price premium on Chef's Table dishes over the usual event pricing, so her kitchen reads as a cut above standard stock. Default 1.25x.
Every so often, Night Owl's kitchen is open. Off by default.
Which NPC mod spawns the people sent after a player who defaults on a loan. With none installed, there are no collectors and the debt gets written off.
Same format as Custom Items (Buy): trader:item:price:max. Example: owl:SomeDrugMod.Cocaine:40:10.

Same format as Custom Items: trader:item:price:qty, semicolon-separated. Example: owl:SomeDrugMod.Cocaine:120:3. Kept separate from Custom Items so it can be toggled off independently (Trade: Contraband above).
Scales how many items every contract asks for. 100 is normal, 25 asks for a quarter. Rewards scale with the amount.

How big job orders get. Pay per item is the same on every setting, so smaller jobs pay less. Easy: up to 10 items, longer deadlines. Medium: up to 15. Hard: up to 20, shorter deadlines, +10 percent pay and more standing.
Hard cap on items per contract. 0 means no cap. Example: 5 means no contract ever asks for more than 5.
Scales how long you get to finish a contract. 100 is normal, 300 gives three times as long.
Traders post jobs for items by a deadline and pay above market. Partners unlock story jobs.
Same format as Custom Items (Sell), but for things the trader will buy from players: trader:item:price:max. Example: ironside:Marz.PulseAmmoBox:15:10.

Let players spend specific items as cash, each at its own fixed value -- useful for gold, silver, or any mod's own currency item. Format: item:value[:rate[:cap]], separated by semicolons. rate is the percent of value actually credited (default 100); cap is the most of that item accepted in a single purchase (default unlimited) -- together they let a trader take something at a discount, as if they 'prefer coins,' and cap how much of a big one-off haul they'll take at once. Defaults to vanilla Gold Coin ($150) and Silver Coin ($25). Gold Bar is deliberately left out -- it isn't trader currency at all, haul it to a known bank and deposit it for Cash instead. Replace or clear the list to use different items, values, rates, or caps entirely. Traders only ever hand back change in regular Cash, never in these items. Leave blank to accept only Cash.

Hand-pick specific items for specific traders instead of relying on auto-detection -- useful for a mod item that doesn't get picked up automatically, or just to curate exactly what a trader carries. Format: trader:item:price:qty, separated by semicolons. Example: ironside:Marz.PulseRifle:250:2;ironside:Marz.PulseAmmoBox:40:6. qty defaults to 5 if left off. Entries for an unknown trader or an item the server doesn't have are silently skipped, same as everything else.
Purchases aren't handed over on the spot. Once an order is ready, the buyer collects it at any mailbox (right-click it > Collect package) and it's dropped at their feet. Off by default.
Biggest discount a broadcast deal can offer. Deals run from 10 below this up to it, for 24 in-game hours, and apply to every player.
Longest in-game delay before an order is ready to collect.
Shortest in-game delay before an order is ready to collect.
When on, trader prices use the multipliers below. When off, everything uses base prices.
For servers running a weapon mod (Guns of Marz, etc): keeps vanilla (Base.*) ammo off every trader's shelf, fixed stock included, so only the mod's own ammo shows up.
Same idea as Exclude Vanilla Ammo, but for the guns themselves: keeps vanilla firearms off every trader's shelf so only a weapon mod's own guns show up.
Percent chance Ironside or Owl pitches a courier/drug run job on a given call, when its toggle above is on. Default 10.
How long after finishing, cancelling, or dying with a Fieldwork job before Ironside or Owl will offer another one. 0 disables the cooldown. Default 6.
Base cash for completing Ironside's courier run, before the distance bonus below. Default 450.
Extra cash added on top of the base pay for both the courier run and the drug run, per 1000 tiles between where you accepted the job and the drop-off. Default 0 (flat pay regardless of distance).
Base cash for completing Owl's drug run, before the distance bonus above. Default 900.
Chance each deposit trips the alarm.
A deposit has a chance to trip a silent alarm that draws nearby zombies toward the box. No new zombies are spawned.
Chance each deposit triggers the ambush.
A deposit has a chance to trigger an armed ambush near the box. Requires the Bandits or Roaming Survivors mod.

Lets Gold Bars be deposited at a physical drop box placed outside each bank. Deposits every Gold Bar carried at once and pays out in Cash Cases, several bars' worth each (see Gold Deposit: Bars Per Payout).
How many Gold Bars' worth of value goes into each payout container.
How much Cash one Gold Bar is worth when deposited. Gold Bars can't be spent as currency or sold to a trader over the radio -- depositing is the only way to cash one in.
Percent chance per call, true night only. Default 2.
Guaranteed condition of the car, overriding the usual random range. Default 70.
How much cheaper than normal. Default 50.
Lets Wrench occasionally offer one used car at a steep discount, late at night. Off by default.
Adds a Make offer button. Odds depend on your standing and how deep the discount is. Push too hard and the trader hangs up.
How loud your calls are to zombies while you wear earbuds or headphones, or have them plugged into a radio you carry. 100 = no change, 25 = a quarter of the normal noise, 0 = silent.
Plays Doc's house call theme while she's on the line. Only you hear it.
Every so often, Doc has something she shouldn't. Off by default.
Lets Ironside occasionally offer a courier run: drive to a distant drop-off, hand a sealed case to his contact in person for a payout. Off by default. Safe -- no combat risk.

Ironside lends money through the Family. Take a loan from his list, get a briefcase of cash, spend it anywhere, and pay it back in full before the deadline. Miss it and armed collectors come for you (needs the Bandits mod; Frockin Wiseguys adds the suits). Without Bandits, defaulting gets you blacklisted instead. Off by default.
Plays Ironside's radio track while Mayhem is on. Only you hear it.
Every so often, Ironside isn't quite himself. Off by default.
Full item IDs traders must never stock or buy, separated by semicolons. Example: Base.Pistol3;GoM.SomeRifle
Chance per call to Night Owl.
Plays Night Owl's late-night track while the back room is open. Only you hear it.

Late at night, Night Owl opens the back room: a short menu of DrugTime89 / Kentucky Cannabis items, and she pays well over her normal price for a few sought-after ones (marked HOT). Only happens if one of those mods is installed. Off by default.
What she pays for HOT items, as a percent of her street price. Her normal buy-back is about 30 percent.
After you miss a deadline, Ironside won't lend to you for this many days. A written-off debt is a permanent ban.
Loan size at Neutral standing. With Reputation on: Regular 2.5x, Trusted 5x, Partner 20x. Distrusted players can't borrow.
Up to this many collectors come each wave, sometimes one fewer.
Waves sent before Ironside writes the debt off and bans you for good. Paying in full stops them.
Missing the deadline sends armed collectors after you. Needs the Bandits mod. Off means defaulting only costs you standing and gets you blacklisted.
Days to repay when Terms is Custom.
Interest in percent when Terms is Custom.
On: missing a deadline sends armed collectors (needs Bandits). Off: missing a deadline just bans you from loans for Loan Ban Days and costs Ironside rep. No one comes for you.
How long you get and how much interest. Lenient: 14 days, 15 percent. Standard: 7 days, 25 percent. Brutal: 3 days, 40 percent. Custom: uses the two settings below.
The most prices can swing up or down.

Selling lots of one item lowers what that trader pays for it (recovers over a few days). After the scheduled power or water shutoff, batteries, fuel, generators and clean water cost more. Temporary power from other mods doesn't count.
The biggest discount a player can ask for.
The most distinct items a trader shows at once, drawn at random from everything they're eligible to trade each restock -- so the shelf is never the same twice. 0 = no cap, show everything eligible.
How much cheaper than normal trade prices. Default 30.
Lets Homestead occasionally sell a batch of alcohol he wants moved quietly. Off by default.
Every so often, Ranger's selling what she shouldn't. Off by default.

Percent chance the drug run turns into an ambush once you're near the drop-off. Needs Bandits2 or Roaming Survivors installed to actually spawn anything -- otherwise the run just stays safe. Default 25.

Lets Owl occasionally offer a drug run: drive a sealed case to a distant drop-off for a bigger payout, with a chance of an ambush once you're close (see Owl Ambush Chance below). You get a warning cue before anything spawns, but this can genuinely get you killed. Off by default.
How long a trader holds a ready package. Not collected in time and it's gone.
How long a delivered parcel (mailbox or airdrop) sits in the world before it's cleaned up, once placed. Default 36.
Some broadcasts announce that Ranger pays extra for gold, silver or gems until tomorrow. The bonus is real and applies to every player.

Nothing ever sells below what that trader pays for it, plus this percent of the asking price, so buying cheap and selling back never profits. Items the trader doesn't buy use 60 percent of the asking price.
What traders CHARGE you. 1.0 = normal, 0.5 = half price, 2.0 = double. Rounds to the nearest dollar, minimum $1.
Set exact base prices for any item. Format: Item=Price, separated by semicolons. Example: Base.Pills=40; Base.Bandage=2. The Base. prefix is optional. Global price multipliers still apply on top.

How often traders pick up. 1.0 = default. Lower is harder (0.5 = noticeably more dead air), higher is easier (2.0 = they usually answer, 3.0 = almost always). It also shortens the wait before a trader who ignored you can be tried again. Trader hours: each trader is only on air at certain hours (shown in the trader list). Off-air traders can still pick up grumpily: about 1 call in 7 at the default 1.0, holding flat up to 2.0, then rising -- about 1 in 3 at 3.0. Weather still weakens the signal.
Cost to be patched through to a trader who is off the air (e.g. Night Owl at midday). If the patch fails, the difference from the normal fee is refunded.
Cost to be patched through to a trader who is currently on the air.
How fast standing goes up. 1.0 = normal.
How fast standing goes down. 1.0 = normal.
Each player earns standing with each trader: Distrusted, Neutral, Regular, Trusted, Partner. Better standing means better prices and more jobs.
How often, in in-game hours, each trader's shelf reshuffles. Default 24 -- once a day. Doesn't affect anything revealed by 'Got anything else?'.
Biggest bonus a rush can pay. Rushes pay from half of this up to it.
Also apply the selling price multiplier to both relay fees.
What traders PAY you. 1.0 = normal, 0.5 = half, 2.0 = double. Worn or used items still pay less. Minimum $1.
Scales service prices. 1.0 = normal. Covers Wrench's gas, battery and propane refills and Sparks' generator repairs.
Wrench refills gas cans and propane tanks and recharges car batteries; Sparks repairs generators (carried, or placed within 3 tiles).
Percent chance per call that Sparks has the side job crate. Default 10.
Sometimes Sparks has a crate of break-in gear: crowbars, bolt cutters, screwdrivers, plus lockpicks and lockpicking books with Neat Lockpicking. Needs Advanced Trading. Off by default.
On: traders stop stocking auto-detected vanilla and mod items. Only items you add in Custom Items (and items other mods register through the API) are sold.
Whether bags and backpacks can show up in Threads' stock or buy list at all. Off removes them entirely instead of just pricing them higher.

Restricts what clothing Threads stocks and buys. Everything: normal behavior, every clothing mod plus vanilla. Vanilla Only: just vanilla (Base.*) clothing, no mods. Authentic Z Only: just Authentic Z's clothing, nothing vanilla or from any other mod.
Percent chance per call, late at night only. Default 2.

Force a specific item list for Threads' night event instead of auto-detecting the supported clothing mods. Format: a semicolon-separated list of full item ids. Example: Base.TrenchCoat;Base.Fedora. Leave blank to use whichever supported mods are active.
At night, Threads may offer her modded clothing rack instead of her usual stock -- requires at least one of the supported clothing mods active, or an item list set below.
Turn off to take DOC off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.
Turn off to take HOMESTEAD off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.
Turn off to take IRONSIDE off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.
Turn off to take NIGHT OWL off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.
Turn off to take RANGER off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.
Turn off to take SPARKS off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.
Turn off to take THREADS off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.
Turn off to take WRENCH off the air completely: never answers, isn't listed, can't be reached by relay. Item category settings are not changed.

On: cash spawns inside an actual wallet item on the corpse (default). Off: cash drops loose into the corpse's own inventory instead, with no wallet container. Turn this off if mass-looting many corpses (e.g. with an auto-loot mod) is causing lag, since each wallet is a separate container that has to be opened and scanned on its own.
Percent chance for a killed zombie to be carrying a wallet with cash in it (0-100). Replaces the vanilla wallet spawn chance so a corpse doesn't end up with two.
Maximum amount of money (in dollars) found in a zombie's wallet, when one drops.
Minimum amount of money (in dollars) found in a zombie's wallet, when one drops.
Optional: lets a zombie's wallet very rarely also contain a scratch card from the Instant Lottery / ScratchCards mod. Off by default. Does nothing and causes no errors if that mod isn't installed.

How much rain, snow, fog, wind and storms interfere with radio signal. 1.0 = normal, 0 = weather never affects transmission, 3.0 = severe. Wired sets (ham/CB base stations) ignore most of this regardless.

Wrench sells beaters: used cars from every installed vehicle mod (Ki5 and friends included), 30 to 60 percent condition, a quarter tank of gas and the key. The car is dropped on open ground about 45 tiles (adjustable) from you.
Chance a killed zombie is carrying loose coins (Gold or Silver Coin), separate from the wallet/cash chance above. Set to 0 to disable.
Most coins dropped when the chance above hits.
Fewest coins dropped when the chance above hits.
Of the coins a zombie drops, the chance each individual one is a Gold Coin instead of a Silver Coin.
Military-grade internals in a civilian shell. Cuts through bad weather other radios can't.
10 Money Bundles wrapped in rubber bands. $1,000. Counts as cash when trading.
Sealed. Not yours to open -- just yours to deliver.
Coordinates, scrawled in a hurry. Ironside will remind you if you lose track.
One dose. Doc says it clears the Knox infection.
Sealed. Best not to ask what's inside.
Coordinates, scrawled in a hurry. Owl will remind you if you lose track.
A trader's delivery. Only the buyer can open it.
You need $%1 for the airdrop fee.
Package dropped. It's at your feet.
Package dropped. It's at your feet. More is still on the way.
It came down about %1 tiles out.
What you're carrying isn't worth enough for that trade.
You don't have any tradeable bulk ammo on you.
Raiders are coming for your money!
Deal alerts on air: %1 MHz (tune in to hear them)
Deal alerts air on %1 MHz. Tune any radio there to hear them.
Stay off the main roads after dark. Keep your antenna up.
Traders are still on the air. Bring cash.
If you can hear this, you're not alone out there.
Check your batteries before you head out.
%1 is moving %2 at %3 percent off until tomorrow. Call in.
%1 has work for anyone who can deliver. Check in on the radio.
Grid's down for good. Batteries, fuel and generators are going for a premium.
%1: paying %2 percent more for gemstones until tomorrow. Diamonds, rubies, emeralds, sapphires. Call in.
%1: paying %2 percent more for gold until tomorrow. Rings, chains, bars, the lot. Call in.
%1: paying %2 percent more for silver until tomorrow. Call in.
Taps are dry. Clean water and purification tablets cost more now.
Bounty expired. Ironside is not happy.
The debtors are close. Watch yourself.
Ironside's opinion of you went up.
Bounty taken. They're holed up in the trailer park near %1.
Two clowns in a trailer park owe me. Make them stop owing. $%1.
Guy with the gold chain and his buddy with the mouth skipped out on me. $%1 when it's done.
Trailer park. The loud ones. You'll hear them before you see them. $%1.
They won't show you anything extra until you've earned some trust.
%1 says there's nothing else worth mentioning right now.
Paid $%1. A few more things turn up (marked with *).
Car bought for $%1. It's parked about %2 tiles from you, key's in your pocket.
No room to drop a car near you. Find some open ground and call back.
She's got some miles on her, but she runs. Mostly.
Key's yours. Don't ask about the smell.
Quarter tank, bald tires. She'll get you somewhere.
Grid's down, so the card machine's dead. Cash only today.
No power, no phone line, no card reader. Cash.
Reader keeps saying 'call center'. Nobody's at the call center. Cash only.
Network's busy, can't get an approval. Cash today.
Storm knocked the phone line out. Can't run cards. Cash only.
Card machine won't dial out in this weather. Cash, please.
I should hold the radio in my hand.
I should hold the radio, or have it holstered on my belt.
I'm too far from that radio now.
A click on the line, then silence. Try again later.
Come on out! We just wanna talk!
Bonus: %1, waiting for you at any mailbox.
They didn't pick up last time -- won't answer a direct call again for a while. A relay through someone else can still get through.
Dead air. Nobody's on the air at this hour. Traders keep set hours -- check the list, or relay through someone who's on.
Nobody said nothing about paying back!
This is %1. Anyone out there? Looking to trade.
Keeps clinic hours. Mornings and afternoons.
This had better be an emergency. What do you need?
Medicine costs. I can't give it away.
I can't treat good intentions. Bring cash.
Clean the wound before you use that.
Done. Don't make me regret it.
Sent. Use it before the wound gets worse, not after.
This is Doc. Keep it brief, I have patients.
Hart here. Are you hurt, or buying?
Hart speaking. Quickly now, who's hurt?
I have enough of those for now.
My shelves are already stocked with those.
You have nothing I can use in that condition.
Nothing usable in what you're carrying.
Transferring you now. Stay on the line.
No answer. I've returned most of your fee.
These will save someone. Thank you.
Payment sent. Clean supplies, I hope.
Good condition. That'll help someone tonight.
I'm out. Try again after my next supply run.
Cabinet's bare. Come back after my rounds.
Your dead drop is in, beside the mailbox nearest where you ordered.
Your dead drop just landed at your feet.
My parcel should be there by now.
A dead-drop parcel was never collected. It's gone.
Added to your dead drop that's already on the way (about %1 hour(s)). One parcel for everything.
Dead drop: your parcel will be left %1 in about %2 hour(s).
right at your feet when it arrives (no mailbox nearby)
SPARKS: Keep this off the air. I've got a crate of things for getting into places. No questions.
NIGHT OWL: Kitchen's open tonight, hon. Real food. Chef's table.
WRENCH: Working late. Got one that fell off a truck -- half price, runs clean. Don't ask.
DOC: Listen carefully. I have one dose of something experimental. It clears the infection. It isn't cheap.
NIGHT OWL: It's late, sugar. Back room's open. I'm paying top dollar for the good stuff tonight.
HOMESTEAD: Got a fresh batch I need moved quiet, before the neighbors notice. Spirits on tap tonight.
RANGER: Off the record... season's open. Don't ask where it came from.
THREADS: Cat's out of the shop after dark. Got some things I don't keep on the regular rack.

Job accepted. Deliver the case at any post office mailbox or trash bin EXCEPT %1 (too close to where you took the call to count) -- Riverside, Ekron, Brandenburg, the Airport, Northwest Louisville, or Fallas Lake.
Job abandoned. No reward, no penalty.
Too close to where you took the job -- try a different post office.
You don't have the case anymore.
You're near a post office. The case can be dropped off here.
Nothing lined up nearby right now. Try again later.
Package confirmed. Good work -- funds are moving.
Made it back in one piece, huh? Not everyone does. Money's yours.
Something's watching you from the treeline. Survive this, then keep moving -- the case still needs to get there.
Deal. $%1 each for the rest of this call.
They don't trust you enough to bargain.
(That's as low as they'll ever go.)
%1 has had enough. The line goes dead.
No. The price is the price.
I said no. Don't push it.
Last warning. Buy it or get off my channel.
Item lines use this format: trader:Module.Item:price:qty, separated by semicolons. Traders: sparks, doc, ironside, owl, wrench, ranger, homestead.
Example for Custom Items (Sell): sparks:Base.Battery:5:10. Custom Items (Buy) uses the same format; the last number is how many they'll buy.
Contraband Items only appear while Trade: Contraband is on. Turning Contraband off also stops Late Night.
Only Sell Custom Items: trader shelves show only your custom items and items added by other mods. Buying, events and rushes keep working.
Price Overrides use Item=Price. Item Blacklist takes item IDs separated by semicolons. The Trader switches take a trader off the air entirely.
Never paste quote marks into these text settings. A stray " can break the saved settings file and blank your lines.
Optional add-ons ship with the mod: tick Radio Traders x Guns of 93 or Radio Traders x Drugs of 93 in the mod list.
These features depend on the server's settings, so some may be switched off.
Reputation: five standings per trader, from Distrusted to Partner. Yours shows as REP in the call window. Better standing means better prices.
Make an offer to haggle on a price. Push too hard and they hang up on you.
Jobs tab: contracts and story jobs. Services: Wrench refills gas cans, car batteries and propane, and Sparks repairs generators.
Dead drops: orders aren't handed over on the spot. When your package is ready, right-click any mailbox and pick Collect package.
Ironside lends money: pay it back before the deadline. Wrench sells used cars: follow the green arrow to find yours.
Rare events can happen when a trader answers: Doc's House Call, Ranger's Open Season, Night Owl's Chef's Table and Late Night, and Ironside's Mayhem.
Traders announce deals on their own radio frequency. It's shown in your radio's window and on the welcome bulletin. Tune any radio there to listen.
A deal you hear is real: it applies to every player for 24 in-game hours.
Ranger always buys jewelry, gems and precious metals. A gold, silver or gem rush on the radio means she pays extra until the next day.
Any two-way radio with power works: a walkie-talkie in your hand or on your belt, or a ham radio or base station placed in the world. Walkies need a working battery and must be switched on.
Right-click the radio and pick Radio Traders, or use the button in the radio's own window.
Traders keep their own hours and don't always answer. Night Owl only picks up after dark. Better radios and clear weather help; a weak signal garbles the line and can drop the call.
Wrong trader answered, or yours is off the air? Pay whoever is on the line to relay you to someone else.
Buy tab: what the trader has right now. Stock is a fresh random draw every restock, every 24 hours by default.
Secret stock: pay for a peek at a few extra items. It costs more each time you ask in the same call.
Sell tab: what the trader will buy. What you get depends on the item's condition, charge left, or how much food is left.

Walkies and ham radios now glow at night while switched on, and Doc's House Call has its own music.
Fixed a bug that could stop zombies from carrying wallets.
New sandbox option: Zombie Wallet. Turn it off for loose cash instead of a wallet item -- better performance when looting a lot of corpses at once.
New rare event: Sparks' Blackmarket Walkie -- an all-weather radio sold only in the dead of night, off the books.
New rare event: Wrench's Graveyard Shift -- one steeply discounted used car, guaranteed condition, late at night only.
New rare event: Homestead's Moonshine Run -- a temporary alcohol and cigarette sell-off at a real discount.
Dead Drops: added an Airdrop option -- pay a fee to have your order dropped in instead of waiting on a mailbox pickup.
Ranger now stocks real skill books (24 skills, 5 tiers each) and sells a reliable skill-teaching VHS tape -- priced by rarity.
Optional support for Roaming Survivors as a loan-collector source, alongside Bandits2 -- pick one in Sandbox options or leave it on Auto.
Airdrops: a homing marker now points to where the crate landed, and the delivery message tells you how far out.
Wrench's Graveyard Shift car is now tagged [STOLEN] in the trade list.
Fixed: walkie/ham radio static lingering for several seconds after power-off, and a recurring server error when dialing from a ham radio.
Wrench's generator buyback cut from $1500 to $500 each.
New ambience and event music: Night Owl's and Ranger's shops, plus Moonshine Run, Break-in and Graveyard Shift now have their own tracks.
Only Sell Custom Items no longer switches off Ranger's rushes, Late Night, or what traders buy.
Generators sell to Sparks again: carry one in your hands and check his Sell tab.
Translations: updated Russian thanks to the community, plus fixes and missing text in every other language.
New Help window: press Help below, or right-click any radio and pick Radio Traders help.
